messages.author: 7bbcb4cbe7d0bc68
messages.subject: lavaan WARNING: x.idx not supported yet (ignored)
parts:
Dear Group

I am calculating a SEM using a dataset of n=300, using fiml to account for the missing data and MLR to account for the multivariate non-normality of the variables/residuals.

I am getting the following warning which I have not found any information on. I would like to know if it indicates the results I’m getting are somehow invalid.

2: In lav_mvnorm_missing_loglik_samplestats(Yp = lavsamplestats@missing[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: x.idx not supported yet (ignored)

My syntax is as follows

model <-
"#latent variable
PRS=~var1.z+var2.z+var3.z
#regressions
PRS~connectedness
var1.z~biodiversity+bio.control
var2.z~biodiversity+bio.control
restoration ~ PRS + stress + biodiversity+bio.control
"

model.fit <- sem(model=model, data=mydata, missing="fiml",estimator="MLR")
summary(model.fit,  fit.measures=T, standardized=T)

I’m using:
R version 3.4.4 (2018-03-15) and lavaan_0.6-1.1208

I’d be most grateful for any information on what is causing the warning and whether it is a problem. Thanks!

Best, Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan WARNING: x.idx not supported yet (ignored)
parts: I'm wondering if it is only in combination with categorical variables

It does not.  This issue occurs only when using FIML, because that warning is triggered in an internal function (lav_mvnorm_missing_loglik_samplestats) that calculates the log-likelihood for each row of data and allows missing data in each row.  Notice that this happens even with complete data:

sem('visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 ; visual ~ sex',
    data = HolzingerSwineford1939, missing = "fiml")

It also only occurs when you treat exogenous observed variables as having fixed sample statistics (above, sex is exogenous; in your original example, connectedness, stress, biodiversity, and bio.control are exogenous).  The warning does not occur if you have no exogenous predictors:

sem('visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3',
    data = HolzingerSwineford1939, missing = "fiml")

nor if you treat them as random variables (with estimated rather than fixed sample statistics)

sem('visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 ; visual ~ sex',
    data = HolzingerSwineford1939, missing = "fiml", fixed.x = FALSE)

I think the warning is harmless, but I think it is there because lavaan used to use listwise deletion for exogenous predictors when fixed.x = TRUE (because you say they are not random multivariate-normal variables whose parameters can be estimated), even if you set missing = "FIML".  But in the development version, using FIML appears to retain the full sample even when fixed.x = TRUE:

HS <- HolzingerSwineford1939
HS$sex[1] <- NA
sem('visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 ; visual ~ sex', data = HS,
    missing = "fiml", fixed.x = TRUE) # N = 301
sem('visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3 ; visual ~ sex', data = HS,
    missing = "fiml", fixed.x = FALSE) # N = 301

So perhaps this warning will not appear by the time this version of lavaan goes to CRAN...

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
